definition: Learning structure from data that has no labels, such as clustering, density estimation or representation learning.
details: Without ground-truth answers, unsupervised methods discover patterns — grouping similar points, compressing data, or predicting parts of the input from the rest. Self-supervised pre-training of language models is a form of this, since the “labels” (the next word) come from the data itself.

explainer.lead: Unsupervised learning finds structure in data that has no labels. It matters because most data arrives unlabelled, and it underpins how language models are pre-trained.

tiers.eli5: Instead of being told the right answers, the model looks at a big pile of examples and sorts out what goes with what.
tiers.practitioner: Used for clustering, density estimation and representation learning; self-supervised pre-training predicts parts of the input from the rest. Pitfall: without ground truth, evaluating whether the learned structure is meaningful is hard.
tiers.paperLevel: Learning from data without target labels, e.g. clustering, density estimation or representation learning; self-supervised variants derive labels from the data itself, such as the next word.

explainer.example: A language model is pre-trained by predicting the next word in text, where the 'label' is simply the following word.
